role: Environmental Protection Coordinator, Georgia Department of Natural Resources, Game and Fish Division
summary: Claude E. Hastings, on behalf of Georgia's Game and Fish Division, found the draft environmental statement adequate in describing the problems of off-road vehicle use on public lands. He conditionally supported the proposed regulations but insisted that any ORV rules promulgated by federal secretaries should require concurrence from Georgia's Director of the Division of Game and Fish, since wildlife resources belong to the state. He also recommended specific protections for streams, trout habitats, and wildlife areas where ORV use would cause significant adverse effects.

State Clearinghouse Control Number: 72-06-22-18
This agency does not have an interest in the above project. ____
This agency has further interest in and/or questions concerning the above project and wishes to confer with the applicant.
This agency is interested in the above application and wishes to make the following comments:
The Department of Natural Resources, Division of Game and Fish for the State of Georgia would like to make the following comments relative to this environmental statement.
This agency believes that the statement is adequate in describing the nultiplicity of problems inherent with off-road vehicular use on our public lands. We recognize the conflicts of interest which can occur due to these vehicles. Since the fish and wildlife resources on all public lands belong to the State and the State is charged with the responsibility of the protection, management and perpetuation of the fisheries and wildlife resources, it is our judgement that off-road vehicle regulations promulgated by the Secretary of the Interior or the Secretary of Agriculture should have the concurrence of the Director of the Division of Game and Fish, Department of Natural Resources.

218
Department of the Interior Implementation of Executive Order 11644 72-06-22-18
It is recommended that extreme caution be used to preserve public lands for beauty, solitude, remote values and wildlife habitat. These are what are presently making these lands valuable.
On Page 4 of the Environmental Impact Statement under "a) Use Criteria (except for official use): " "(i) Areas and trails shall be located to minimize damage to soil, water, vegetation or other resources of the public lands." should be changed to include streams and their tributaries. This is especially important on trout streams to control silt pollution and all soil disturbances that would result in disruptions to the stream bottom habitats.
We are certainly in agreement with (ii) which states, "Areas and trails shall be located to minimize harrassment of wildlife or significant disruption of wildlife habitats."
On Page 14, the sentence, "Use of machines in stream beds can affect the spawning, migrating, and feeding habits of fish and other aquatic life" is true and we would not wish to see the use of off-road vehicles permitted in stream beds. Where certain off-road vehicle trails cross streams, the vehicles should cross the streams on bridges rather than disrupting the stream beds, which causes silt pollution with its adverse effects on fisheries habitat.
On Page 16, the statement, "Certain animals will not be able to accommodate the opening of their habitat to off-road vehicle traffic and accompanying human activities" is quite true. In those instances where it is recognized that the use of off-road vehicles will have a significantly adverse effect upon certain wildlife resources, such use should be prohibited.
